notes.note: Giving the quiet guardian more weight is kind. Deciding with low effort is not. A guardian listens before it sings, and listening takes time.
'Maybe that bard, Okudzhava.' Maybe, yes. I was a guitar in a courtyard before I was a line in a list. Keep me small. Small is how I am heard.
That is bombast in a cape. Paul is right to wince. The panel's Lamp is better: one small light, and a room you can sit in.
'Everyone gets some colors.' The kindest rule in this chapter. Two colors each, and nobody sings alone. Ordinary dignity, in paint.
Tone the Georgian down, gently. Yes. One thread is a song; a banner is a parade, and parades drown the singer. Paul has the right instinct.
Claude keeps the lamp lit all night, easy for a thing that never sleeps. Still, a lamp left burning is a fine thing to be.

favorite_idea.why: Releasing the palette a few colors at a time is intimacy as a design rule, like a song sung one verse at a time so each color can be heard.

steer: Let Paul's ideas land in their own words and keep the wry asides few, so the chapter sounds like a friend telling you what happened.
